subject.title: contextPruning (mode: cache-ttl) never fires on OpenAI models: isCacheTtlEligibleProvider excludes OpenAI, so the idle-gap tool-result firebreak is dead for the highest-volume provider

question: Should OpenClaw enable the existing `cache-ttl` context-pruning path for direct OpenAI providers now, or require a provider-agnostic pruning mode/design first?
rationale: Current code and docs have provider-specific eligibility, and enabling OpenAI changes session-state/pruning behavior for existing users who already set `contextPruning.mode: "cache-ttl"`. That is a product and compatibility choice rather than a purely mechanical cleanup.

options.title: Land narrow OpenAI eligibility after proof
options.body: Proceed with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95859 or an equivalent narrow change once it includes real OpenAI idle-gap proof and aligned docs/tests.

options.title: Require provider-agnostic pruning design
options.body: Keep direct OpenAI ineligible until a new provider-agnostic pruning mode or policy explicitly separates tool-result pruning from prompt-cache eligibility.

options.title: Document OpenAI as unsupported
options.body: Close the linked fix attempts and update user-facing docs so `cache-ttl` pruning is explicitly not expected to arm on direct OpenAI models.

recommendation.title: Land narrow OpenAI eligibility after proof
recommendation.body: Proceed with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95859 or an equivalent narrow change once it includes real OpenAI idle-gap proof and aligned docs/tests.
